newsitem.title: USA: Liberian-flagged oil tanker strikes Maine bridge.
newsitem.headline: Liberian-flagged oil tanker strikes Maine bridge.

text.p: Emergency crews scrambled to clean up an estimated 600 barrels of oil that leaked from a Liberian-registered tanker that struck a drawbridge on Friday, officials said.

The 560-foot (170-meter) Julie N was entering Portland Harbor with a cargo of approximately 210,000 barrels of No. 2 distillate fuel when it struck a granite abutment on a bridge across the harbor, officials said.

The cause of the accident was not immediately known. Seas were calm and winds light but the 85-foot-wide ship (25-meter) was trying to make it through the bridge's 95-foot (28-meter) opening, officials said
"The difficulty of the approach to the Portland bridge is well known," Coast Guard Commander Burton Russell told reporters. The ship had a harbor pilot on board at the time of the accident, he said.

The accident punched holes in two of the ship's tanks, spilling both distillate fuel from the load and bunker oil used by the ship into the water. The total spill was estimated at 600 barrels but the exact amount was not known.

The Coast Guard said both leaks had stopped. The heavier oil was contained around the now docked ship, but lighter distillate could seen and smelled around the harbor. The lighter fuel was expected to evaporate in the next few days.

Officials said the size of the spill was reduced both because of the quick response of emergency crews and the captain's decision to dock at a nearby oil terminal which had pollution control booms to trap the bunker oil.

The Coast Guard closed Portland harbor and ordered the autoferry Scotia Prince, which runs daily between Portland and Yarmouth, Nova Scotia to divert to Bar Harbor. Lobster fishing in the harbor area was banned.

The accident left Portland with both an environmental and transportation problem. The 80-year-old drawbridge is a major commuter route and is now stuck in the open position because of broken electrical cables and bent metal.
Gov. Angus King said the bridge would be repaired even though a larger replacement drawbridge is being built and scheduled to open next summer.

The Julie N is owned by New York-based Maritime Overseas Corp, a unit of Overseas Shipholding Group Inc, a company official said. It was chartered by Global Petroleum Corp. and scheduled to discharge its load at Sprague Oil in Portland.
